messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone!

As you might have heard, the 3rd International Ecoacoustics Congress will be held in Brisbane from June 24th-28th. This is a dual spam message :)

1. Abstracts are open until Feb 11th, so if you haven't submitted, please join the fun.
2. Is anyone interested in teaching a seewave/monitoR course there? I would be happy to do this, but feel like a bit of an impostor, with only about 18 months of experience... so if there would be a co-convener that would be fantastic. Please let me know in the next few weeks

Simon

messages.subject_clean: Error in covspectro when estimating covariance of two waves
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to batch analyze a bunch of blue tit calls. Part of my analysis is related to the similarity among repetitions of the same note. For this I am using several functions including "covspectro".
Some times and with no apparent reason I get this error message:

"Error in spectro2b[, , which(step2 == i)] <- sspectro(wave = as.matrix(c(rep(0,  :
  número de items para para sustituir no es un múltiplo de la longitud del reemplazo"

English translation:
"Error in spectro2b[, , which(step2 == i)] <- sspectro(wave = as.matrix(c(rep(0,  :
  the number of items to substitute is not multiple of the length of the replacement"

I have been trying to understand why this happens and how to solve it but I am definitely frustrated right now.

To make sure that both waves are the same duration I paste a wave of silence or cut wave. I wrote this code:

if (duration(note1_f) != duration(note2_f)){

    if (duration(note1_f) > duration(note2_f)){

       silence_add <- cutw(silence, f = sil...@samp.rate, to = (duration(note1_f) - duration(note2_f)), output = 'Wave')

       note2_f_covspec <- pastew(silence_add, note2_f, f = f, output = 'Wave', join = F)}

if (duration(note1_f) < duration(note2_f)){

    note2_f_covspec <- cutw(note2_f, f = f, to = (duration(note2_f) - (duration(note2_f) - duration(note1_f))), output = 'Wave')}}else{}

I would love to have some insight from the outside! I thing there is something I cannot see.

Kind regards,
Javi

messages.subject: problem removing offset
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I'm processing files recorded with SM3 and SM4 recorders, both affected by offset, that is different in the two channels.

In R/Seewave I'm doing this

        soundfile=readWave(filename)
        waveL=channel(soundfile,which="left")    # split the stereo wave in two mono wave objects
        waveR=channel(soundfile,which="right")
        rmoffset(waveL, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)
        rmoffset(waveR, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)

however my waveL and waveR still have their original offset and I see it any plot

I also tried with this script:

        CleanL=rmoffset(waveL, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)
        CleanR=rmoffset(waveR, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)

but when I then use

  spectro(CleanL, osc=TRUE)

I get an error message saying that CleanL is not a wavs object

Are there others with the same problem ?   Or I'm wrong somewhere ?

Gianni

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] saving a spectrogram
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gianni,

I am not sure to understand you request. If you mean that you wish to save the matrix of the spectrogram, you can do something like:

# get the spectro matrix
data(tico)
m <- spectro(tico, plot=FALSE)$amp
# save it as a csv file
write.table(m, file="tico-spectro.csv")

HTH

Jerome

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jerome,

I think I found the problem, it may have to do with the pastew or cutw function. As I said I was pasting a small wave of silence to lengthen the wave2 if it was shorter than wave1. I haven't narrowed down the mistake to the specific place but I solved it by cutting the waves 0.005 seconds shorter than they should. Maybe there was something wrong with the joint.

I can have a closer look if you want more details but so far I fixed my problem.

Thank you for the fast support anyway!
Kind regards
Javi

messages.body_plain:
Ok, use the function pdf() then, for instance :

data(tico)
d <- duration(tico)
time <- seq(0, d, by=d/4)

pdf("spectro.pdf")
for(i in 1:(length(time)-1))
    {
       spectro(tico, tlim=c(time[i], time[i+1]))
        }
dev.off()

But be carefull the final pdf might be bery heavy.

Best

Jerome

In the manual (spectro -> dBref) it says it uses a 20 mPa reference value. Which correction factor should i use to calculate from dB to, lets say tesla or nanoTesla? Or nothing logarithmical is suppose? Im very confused.

Thank you for your thoughts.

Hey guys,

I'm new to Seewave R package, and have never worked with R language before.

Any practical guidance someone could give me?

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Starting to use own audio files
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Starting to use own audio files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tiago,

In general the process is the same as loading any file into R. You use a specific function (here it would be readWave()) and tell it where to look for the file.

File locations trip up a lot of new R users. I would suggest checking out some tutorials which explain the ideas of a working directory, and projects (if you're using Rstudio). This resource looks like a good place to start: https://www.stat.ubc.ca/~jenny/STAT545A/block01_basicsWorkspaceWorkingDirProject.html#workspace-and-working-directory

Once you understand how to refer to the location of a file, you need to use the readWave() function which is explained here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/seewave/vignettes/seewave_IO.pdf#subsubsection.1.3.1

I hope this helps get you started,

Steffi
Dr. Stefanie LaZerte
Biologist, R and CitSci Enthusiast
http://steffilazerte.ca/
